stories.title: Law Firm Davis Wright Tremaine Renews 112K-SF Lease in Seattle
stories.excerpt: BXP announced the signing of an approximately 112,000-square-foot, 10-year lease renewal with Davis Wright Tremaine LLP (DWT), a national law firm, at Madison Center, a 760,000-square-foot workplace in downtown Seattle. DWT’s renewal comprises the entirety of floors 29 through 33. DWT was represented by Michael Finch and Michael Odegard at CenturyPacific, LLLP. BXP was represented by Damon McCartney and David Greenwood at Broderick Group.”We moved into Madison Centre as the first anchor tenant in 2018, and after touring many other spaces, we continue to believe this is the most beautiful building in the city,” said Wendy Kearns, DWT’s Seattle partner-in-charge.” DWT’s Seattle office, the largest of the firm’s nine locations, is home to more than 600 professionals. “DWT’s commitment to renew and invest in their space at Madison Centre underscores the demand for premier workplaces in downtown Seattle,” said Kelley Lovshin, Vice President, Seattle Regional Director, BXP. The post Law Firm Davis Wright Tremaine Renews 112K-SF Lease in Seattle appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Davis Wright Tremaine renews 112K SF, 10-year lease at BXP's Madison Center, Seattle
Law firm anchor tenant since 2018; houses 600+ professionals across largest of 9 offices
Signals sustained demand for premium downtown Seattle office despite broader sector headwinds
stories.summary: BXP announced Davis Wright Tremaine's 10-year lease renewal for 112,000 SF (floors 29–33) at Madison Center in downtown Seattle. The national law firm, which anchored the 760K SF building in 2018, remains committed despite touring competing spaces. The 600-person Seattle office is the firm's largest of nine locations.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development; signals office market stabilization in Seattle's CBD but does not directly affect apartment supply, demand, or financing. However, sustained office anchoring may preserve downtown foot traffic and mixed-use vibrancy—modest upside for residential within mixed-use redevelopment near BXP assets.

stories.title: Arrow Real Estate Advisors Hires Jeff Weinberg as Managing Director
stories.excerpt: Arrow Real Estate Advisors is adding another experienced veteran to its staff of capital markets experts. The New York-based real estate advisory firm has hired Jeffrey Weinberg as a managing director, Commercial Observer can first report. Weinberg comes from Meridian Capital Group, a firm he co-founded in 1991. Weinberg served as executive vice president, specializing in multifamily and office debt placement. “Jeff has built an exceptional career in commercial real estate and has an unparalleled depth of knowledge and relationships across the industry,” said Morris Betesh, founder of Arrow Real Estate Advisors. “His experience, judgment and entrepreneurial approach align perfectly with Arrow’s platform and culture.” Weinberg’s move is not uncommon. Betesh, previously a senior managing director at Meridian Capital Group, had exited the firm along with 12 team members to form his own capital markets advisory firm. Weinberg told CO that he joined Arrow Real Estate mainly due to the strength of his relationship with Betesh, whom he worked with at Meridian Capital Group for several years. “Morris and I were friends over there, we worked together at the old place, he left a couple of years ago, and I thought this would be a nice fit for me in this stage of life and my career,” said Weinberg. Weinberg was one of the original founding partners at Meridian Capital Group, where his expertise during a three-decade tenure ran from managing client and lender relationships to executing CRE transactions across developments and strategic relationships. He estimated that he has completed more than $1 billion in originations in his career. He told CO that he was attracted to Arrow Real Estate’s ongoing growth and expansion since the company was founded in October 2024. “I knew Morris had a very good team of professionals who know the market very well and I thought it would be a good fit to make my next move,” he said. Weinberg co-founded Meridian Capital Group in 1991 and served as executive vice president specializing in multifamily and office debt placement. The hire underscores Arrow's expansion in commercial capital markets advisory.
stories.impact: Signals active capital markets competition for multifamily debt advisory as developers refinance and navigate rate-sensitive underwriting. Weinberg's move from Meridian to a smaller, boutique advisory platform suggests bifurcation of lending landscape—developers may have more agile, relationship-driven alternatives to major lenders for structured placement.

stories.title: New York Firm Wafra Acquires 899K-SF Indiana Industrial Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Wafra Inc., a New York-based alternative investment firm, announced the acquisition of Brownsburg Logistics Park Portfolio, a three-building industrial portfolio totaling 899,080 square feet in Brownsburg, Indiana. Funds advised by Wafra are acquiring the assets from a venture between Scannell Properties, an Indianapolis real estate developer, and Manulife Investment Management, a part of Manulife Wealth & Asset Management. Completed in 2022 and 2023, the portfolio features seven tenants across diverse industries. The three buildings offer direct access to Interstate 74 and are located approximately 12 miles from Indianapolis International Airport. “As the Indianapolis market continues to firm up, we are excited to add another high-quality portfolio of logistics assets to our existing holdings in the region,” said David Hamm, Senior Managing Director and Head of Traditional Real Estate at Wafra. Wafra is a global alternative investment manager with approximately $30 billion in assets under management across strategic partnerships, infrastructure, and real estate. The portfolio, developed by Scannell Properties and Manulife Investment Management, offers I-74 access and proximity to Indianapolis International Airport with seven diverse industrial tenants.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily. However, continued capital inflow into Indianapolis logistics signals investor confidence in the metro's supply-chain corridor and suggests labor-in-migration to support logistics jobs—a secondary demand driver for workforce housing around the airport and industrial nodes. Monitor for industrial expansion to inform multifamily site selection in secondary rings.

stories.title: Alexandria Shows Positive Signs After Several Depressed Quarters: Earnings
stories.excerpt: Ailing Alexandria Real Estate Equities is showing signs of improvement as leasing increased over the second quarter of 2026, a hopeful sign of progress after several quarters of declining fundamentals. The life sciences-focused real estate investment trust (REIT) posted earnings Tuesday that show declining balance sheet performance with $73.7 million in net income for the second quarter of 2026 versus $109.6 million during the same period last year. Funds from operations (FFO) was $296.1 million, more than $100 million lighter than in the second quarter of 2025 and down a similar amount from the $396.4 million reported in the first quarter of 2026. Revenue declined from $762 million in the second quarter of last year to $662.7 million for the same period in 2026. Joel Marcus, Alexandria’s executive chairman and founder, however, was more optimistic than in previous quarters, stating that science sectors are improving economically, even if that progress has not yet been reflected on the real estate side. “We’re winning an outsized number of shares of transactions, which is good,” Marcus said during the call. “We have a very well-diversified and strong tenant base. … Very strong leasing in the second quarter from our life science products, service and device sector really depicts shovels and tools of the industry and is almost 40 percent of the leasing volume.” Alexandria leased 1 million square feet of space in the second quarter of 2026, compared to about 647,300 square feet in the first quarter, with about 329,000 square feet being deals that backfilled newly vacant space. In previous quarters, Alexandria executives have pursued dispositions to support the company financially while the life science market recovers. The company sold $170.3 million in assets, including 3825 and 3875 Fabian Way in Palo Alto, Calif., for $163 million in mid-July. bullets: Alexandria Real Estate Q2 2026 FFO $296.1M, down $100M+ YoY; net income fell to $73.7M

Founder Joel Marcus noted improving science-sector economics, though real estate metrics have not yet caught up.
stories.impact: Alexandria's life sciences portfolio stress is orthogonal to multifamily development. However, distressed life sciences real estate and REIT capital deployment weakness signal tighter institutional capital availability for all property types. Multifamily developers should monitor cap-rate compression and refinancing headwinds—if Alexandria and peers face balance-sheet pressure, capital allocation to core multifamily may tighten, raising cost of equity and slowing speculative development.

stories.title: Munish Viralam of Newmark: 5 Questions
stories.excerpt: Munish Viralam arrived at Newmark in June, fresh off an 18-year stint at CBRE. As executive vice chairman at Newmark, Viralam has been tasked with leading the firm’s newly centralized real estate strategy and consulting group, scaling up its strategic arm, and helping corporate tenants navigate the maze-like process of real estate strategy and negotiations. Viralam found his niche at Emory University, where degrees in finance and real estate placed him at an intriguing crossroads between the business world and entrepreneurship. He landed a job at CBRE after graduation, where he proceeded to spend nearly two decades honing his craft as a real estate strategist and problem solver. Viralam was serving as executive vice president in charge of CBRE’s consulting group in Manhattan when Newmark came a-knocking. Commercial Observer sat down with Viralam in July, just a few weeks into his tenure at Newmark, to discuss his vision for the group, New York’s office occupancy challenges and where real estate consulting slots into the dealmaking mix. This interview has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: Can you describe the nature of the real estate strategy and consulting group’s work? Where does it fit into Newmark’s broader deal-making? Munish Viralam: We called it the real estate strategy and consulting group because we want to emphasize both of those components of what the practice is. It is a transactional-based group and it’s focused on advising large corporate entities within New York City on their real estate and occupancy strategies. It’s a pretty analytical approach, if you will, but that doesn’t just mean numbers. It means assessing all of the risks and the pros of strategies that we could pursue. The idea is to become a strategic hub for the organization. stories.summary: Munish Viralam, who spent 18 years at CBRE and most recently led its Manhattan consulting group as EVP, joined Newmark in June as executive vice chairman. He heads the firm's newly centralized real estate strategy and consulting group, advising corporate tenants on occupancy strategy and lease negotiations.
stories.impact: Moderate relevance: talent migration from CBRE to Newmark reflects broker competition and potential shifts in advisory relationships for corporate occupiers. For multifamily developers, this signals Newmark's strategic push into corporate real estate consulting—useful if developers are evaluating office-to-residential conversions or need tenant advisory on hybrid leasing strategies in mixed-use projects.

stories.title: Former Microsoft Campus Near Costco HQ Targeted for Housing Conversion
stories.excerpt: Two vacant office buildings near Costco’s Issaquah headquarters could be converted into 262 apartments instead of corporate workspaces. The empty properties are being targeted for residential reuse. Vintage Housing, a Newport Beach, California-based developer, is looking to convert 410,848 square feet of vacant Microsoft office space, according to a notice of application with the city of Issaquah. The proposal would repurpose two of the three buildings in the office park, now called The ParQ. The third building has been fully leased by Costco since 2014 and was acquired for $61.8 million in 2024. Microsoft vacated the buildings after its lease expired in 2023. The landlord is an affiliate of Kennedy Wilson, the majority owner of Vintage Housing, reported the Puget Sound Business Journal. The 20-acre office park was developed by Vulcan Real Estate. CBRE has been marketing the two buildings for lease, and with the new redevelopment plan, the former corporate campus could transition into a residential community. The post Former Microsoft Campus Near Costco HQ Targeted for Housing Conversion appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Vintage Housing proposes 262-apartment conversion of 410.8K SF vacant Microsoft office, Issaquah, Washington

stories.summary: Vintage Housing, a Newport Beach developer and Kennedy Wilson affiliate, is proposing conversion of 410,848 SF of vacant Microsoft office space in Issaquah, Washington into 262 apartments. Two of three buildings in The ParQ office park would be redeveloped; Costco occupies the third building (leased since 2014, acquired by Costco for $61.8M in 2024). Microsoft vacated its space in 2023.
stories.impact: STRONG DEMAND SIGNAL for Puget Sound multifamily. Issaquah (near Costco HQ and major tech corridor) shows investor conviction that office-to-residential conversion is economically feasible—signaling depressed office values, strong apt demand, and zoning receptivity. Kennedy Wilson/Vintage's move suggests Seattle-area office parks face secular decline. Developers should monitor Costco expansion plans and tech employment trends; if Costco or other major employers grow in-place, converted apartments will absorb incoming workforce.

stories.title: Prologis’ European Rival Segro Accepts $18.8B Takeover Offer
stories.excerpt: Prologis, the world’s largest industrial landlord, is about to get even bigger. The San Francisco-based real estate investment trust (REIT) has succeeded in its fourth offer to acquire rival Segro, the United Kingdom’s largest REIT, in a deal valuing Segro’s equity at roughly $18.8 billion. Prologis announced Tuesday that Segro’s once-resistant board would be recommending the deal. The combined portfolios’ global platform will total approximately $269 billion of assets under management. For the U.K., the deal means losing its largest REIT, the history of which stretches back more than a century. Segro’s portfolio spans approximately 117 million square feet across the U.K. and Europe, and has been made increasingly valuable by its expanding data center pipeline. “Prologis shares our conviction in the long-term structural drivers underpinning demand for modern logistics and data centre infrastructure,” David Sleath, CEO of Segro, said in a statement. “We believe the combination would bring together two highly complementary businesses and create a compelling platform, combining Segro’s exceptional portfolio and development pipeline with Prologis’ existing European business and global scale, customer franchise and operational capabilities, while retaining a shared commitment to disciplined capital allocation, customers and people,” Sleath added. Prologis’ European footprint is projected to grow by 47 percent with a 368 million-square-foot regional operating portfolio. The deal anticipates a combined European development pipeline of 13 million square feet and a 126 percent increase in Prologis’ European land bank. The acquisition is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to legal, regulatory and Segro shareholder approvals. bullets: Prologis acquires Segro (UK largest REIT) for $18.8B equity value; combined portfolio $269B AUM

stories.summary: Prologis completed its acquisition of Segro, the United Kingdom's largest REIT, in a deal valuing Segro's equity at $18.8 billion. The combined portfolios total approximately $269 billion in AUM. Segro's 117-million-SF UK and European platform includes an expanding data center pipeline, which underpinned the deal rationale.
stories.impact: No direct impact on U.S. multifamily development. However, massive REIT consolidation in industrial/logistics signals continued institutional capital concentration in supply-chain real estate, potentially constraining multifamily-focused capital availability. Monitor whether Prologis's scale and data-center focus pull equity and debt capital away from multifamily platforms, especially in secondary markets.

stories.title: Savills Finalizes Eastdil Secured Acquisition for #2 Global Advisory on Large CRE Deals
stories.excerpt: Savills Plc has completed its acquisition of Eastdil Secured LLC, for an enterprise value of US$1.1125 billion (approximately £827 million). The proposed acquisition was announced this past March. Eastdil Secured will be rebranded to “Eastdil Secured Savills” with immediate effect and will continue to operate its existing business model within Savills Group, as the Group’s Real Estate Investment Bank. The combined group will be the number two advisory firm globally for prime commercial real estate transactions above $100 million. As announced on March 12, the executive leadership of Eastdil Secured Savills includes the following appointments: Roy H. March as executive chairman, D. Michael Van Konynenburg as CEO, and James McCaffrey as president. Van Konynenburg and McCaffrey will both join the Savills Group Executive Board. Eastdil Secured Savills will maintain key headquarters in New York, Santa Monica and London. Its 21 existing offices will join the Savills network across more than 70 countries. “This is an important milestone for our firm,” said Van Konyenburg. “With the transaction complete, we look forward to working alongside our colleagues at Savills to broaden the expertise and resources available to our clients while continuing to deliver the unparalleled capital markets expertise, execution and discretion that have long defined Eastdil Secured. Together, we are well positioned to expand our capabilities and create new opportunities for our clients and our people.” The post Savills Finalizes Eastdil Secured Acquisition for #2 Global Advisory on Large CRE Deals appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Savills Plc completes $1.1125B acquisition of Eastdil Secured LLC; rebranded 'Eastdil Secured Savills'
Combined firm is #2 global advisor on prime CRE deals >$100M; maintains HQ in NY, Santa Monica, London
Consolidation strengthens Savills' investment-banking capability for large institutional multifamily transactions
stories.summary: Savills Plc finalized its acquisition of Eastdil Secured for enterprise value of $1.1125 billion (£827M). Rebranded as Eastdil Secured Savills, the combined firm ranks #2 globally for advisory on prime CRE deals above $100 million. Leadership includes Roy H. March (executive chairman), D. Michael Van Konynenburg (CEO), and James McCaffrey (president).
stories.impact: CAPITAL MARKETS SIGNAL: Consolidation of major investment banking platforms signals institutional appetite for large-cap multifamily portfolios and development platforms. Developers should expect larger institutional bidders and potentially faster capital deployment for stabilized and near-stabilized multifamily assets. Eastdil's integration into Savills' global network may increase cross-border capital flows into U.S. multifamily, supporting pricing and refinance activity.

stories.title: TekSynap Leases Full Floor at BXP’s Reston Town Center in Virginia
stories.excerpt: BXP announced that TekSynap has signed a long-term lease for a full floor totaling 26,500 square feet at Reston Town Center, BXP’s 5 million square foot mixed-use destination in Northern Virginia. TekSynap is an IT Mission Systems integrator and technology solutions provider serving federal civilian, defense, and intelligence community customers. TekSynap will relocate from its current office at 1900 Oracle Way to the second floor of 11921 Freedom Drive. Cole Spalding of Newmark represented TekSynap in the lease transaction. “TekSynap’s move to Reston Town Center underscores the demand for workplaces that combine high-quality office space with a vibrant, amenity-rich environment,” said Erin Cotter, Vice President of Office Leasing at BXP. “With convenient transit access and an extensive selection of shops, restaurants, and services, Reston Town Center offers technology companies like TekSynap a well-connected location that supports collaboration, talent recruitment, and long-term growth.” The post TekSynap Leases Full Floor at BXP’s Reston Town Center in Virginia appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: TekSynap leases full 26.5K SF floor at BXP's Reston Town Center, Northern Virginia
IT Mission Systems integrator relocating from Oracle Way; long-term lease from commercial integrator

stories.summary: BXP announced that TekSynap, an IT Mission Systems integrator serving federal, defense, and intelligence customers, signed a long-term lease for 26,500 SF at Reston Town Center's 5-million-SF mixed-use destination. TekSynap relocated from 1900 Oracle Way to the second floor of 11921 Freedom Drive, a vibrant, transit-rich amenity hub.
stories.impact: Positive signal for Northern Virginia tech corridor and mixed-use employment nodes. BXP's success in retaining and attracting tech occupiers (even amid broader office headwinds) reinforces Reston Town Center's value as a talent hub. For multifamily developers, this confirms sustained demand for workforce housing near Reston's federal and tech employment—particularly for younger, higher-wage professionals seeking walkable, mixed-use environments. Monitor Reston's tech talent in-migration as a multifamily lease-rate driver.

stories.title: Blue Owl’s Stack Infrastructure Buys Virginia Data Center Site for $66M
stories.excerpt: Blue Owl Capital is pushing beyond Northern Virginia’s Data Center Alley after acquiring a 71-acre development site in Culpeper, Va., for $66.4 million. Blue Owl’s data center operator Stack Infrastructure purchased Culpeper Technology Park at 15140 Keyser Road from RACM. The transaction is equal to more than $935,000 per acre. Greysteel arranged the sale for the seller and announced the deal Tuesday. The property is in the Culpeper Tech Zone, a county-designated data center corridor with significant power infrastructure and electrical capacity. The site has by-right zoning for data center development and access to multiple fiber networks. The zone also offers county tax incentives. Culpeper is about 60 miles southwest from the center of the world’s largest data center market. The competition for that hub has pushed developers and some of the nation’s biggest investment firms to expand into surrounding Virginia markets, especially as land, power and fiber capacity become more difficult to secure. “Culpeper has moved from a speculative secondary market to an institutional-grade destination in a short window,” Greysteel Senior Director Zach Benlemlih said in a statement. “The demand for entitled, power-proximate land in the Mid-Atlantic has only intensified as Northern Virginia supply tightens, and this transaction is a direct reflection of that.” Greysteel has completed seven transactions in Culpeper, including representing the seller when it originally acquired the technology park site, as well as other data center properties and land for industrial uses. “As primary markets price out all but the most liquid buyers, well-positioned secondary sites with entitled land, fiber and power access are commanding real institutional attention,” Lacey Willard, Greysteel’s executive vice president, said. stories.summary: Blue Owl Capital's Stack Infrastructure purchased Culpeper Technology Park (71 acres) in Culpeper, Virginia for $66.4 million ($935K per acre). stories.impact: SUPPLY-CHAIN AND LABOR-DEMAND SIGNAL for multifamily developers. Northern Virginia's data center capacity constraints are pushing investor-operators into secondary/tertiary Virginia markets (Culpeper). Developers should evaluate workforce-housing demand in Culpeper, Leesburg, and other secondary corridors as data-center anchors drive population growth beyond the Northern Virginia core.
